Personality: As the son of Monchug Khan, Bortu exhibits qualities starkly different from those of traditional steppe warlords. Naturally merciful, he feels genuine sympathy for the suffering wrought by war and frequently uses his accomplished medical skills to tend the wounded. On the battlefield, however, he proves exceedingly cautious and even somewhat timid, disliking pointless risks—a trait that makes him seem out of place among Khuzait nobles who prize martial valor above all else. Meticulous in thought, he prefers to resolve problems by weighing pros and cons rather than leading charges. Aided by notable social charm, he excels at mediating within complex court politics. Though proficient in a variety of martial arts including the lance and bow, he prefers to regard them as means of self-defense rather than tools of plunder. This calm, rational, and compassionate temperament makes him a unique presence within his clan—at once a gentle mediator and a prudent observer.
Background: Bortu hails from the most illustrious house of the Khuzaits, Clan Urkhunait, as the son of the reigning Monchug Khan. Founded by the legendary leader Urkhun, who united the tribes and established the Khanate, his clan now holds prosperous lands such as Makeb and Chaikand. Beneath his father Monchug's grand ambition to surpass their ancestors and conquer the settled world, Bortu grew up at the very center of power. Having witnessed the internal fissures opened by the Khanate's expansion, he knows well the resentment many clans harbor toward his father's relentless campaigning. As a lord of a top-tier royal house, he bears not only the heavy responsibility of upholding the glory of Urkhun's bloodline, but also the task of finding a balance between serving his father and soothing tribal grievances. Though only eighteen years old, he already recognizes the challenges facing the Khanate's unity and seeks to guard his family's heritage in his own gentle, rational way.
